value.title: Subexponential rank-one metric families have zero restricted asymptotic price
value.summary:
Fix a dimension \(n\), an integer \(M\ge 2\), and any finite family of unit
vectors

\[
\mathcal U=\{u_1,\ldots,u_m\}\subset S^{n-1}.
\]

Associate to these vectors the trace-normalized rank-one metrics
\(\Sigma_i=n u_i u_i^{\mathsf T}\). Define the minimax overhead restricted to
this family by

\[
\Pi_n(\mathcal U,M)=
\inf_{\substack{C\subset\mathbb R^n\\ |C|=M}}
\max_{1\le i\le m}
\left[
\frac{\log_2 M}{n}
-R_{\mathrm{wf}}\bigl(\Sigma_i,D(C,\Sigma_i)\bigr)
\right].
\]

Put

\[
\beta_m=4m\sqrt{2\ln(8m)}
\]

and

\[
B(M,m)=
\frac{4\beta_m^2\ln M}{(M-1)^2}
+\frac{2}{\sqrt{2\pi}\,M^2}
\left(2\sqrt{\ln M}+\frac{1}{2\sqrt{\ln M}}\right).
\]

There is an explicit collinear \(M\)-word codebook, depending on
\(\mathcal U\), for which

\[
D(C,\Sigma_i)\le B(M,m)\qquad(1\le i\le m).
\]

Consequently, whenever \(B(M,m)<1\),

\[
0\le \Pi_n(\mathcal U,M)
\le \frac{1}{2n}\log_2\!\bigl(M^2B(M,m)\bigr).
\tag{1}
\]

In particular, let \(R>0\), let \(M_n=\lceil 2^{nR}\rceil\), and allow the
rank-one family \(\mathcal U_n\) to vary with \(n\). If its cardinality
\(m_n\) satisfies

\[
\ln m_n=o(n),
\]

then

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\Pi_n(\mathcal U_n,M_n)=0.
\tag{2}
\]

Thus no fixed, polynomial-size, or more generally subexponential-size family
of differently oriented rank-one metrics can by itself prove a positive
asymptotic minimax price against arbitrary codebooks. Any rank-one
finite-family lower-bound route must use exponentially many orientations (at
the relevant exponent) or add an argument that genuinely controls metrics
outside the displayed family.

Scope qualifications: The family is implicitly nonempty (\(m\ge1\)), as required by \(\beta_m\) and the maximum over orientations. The result concerns only the displayed finite rank-one family; it does not control metrics outside that family or establish zero price for the full uncountable metric class. “Explicit” means that the codebook has a displayed formula after selecting a probabilistically proved witness \(v\); no effective deterministic or efficient witness-construction algorithm is established. Repeated, dependent, or nongeneric orientations are allowed; no independence or general-position assumption is needed.

value.title: Gaussian witness, scalar-grid distortion, and water-filling proof
value.summary: Draw \(G\sim N(0,I_n)\) and apply marginal Gaussian lower-tail and upper-tail bounds with a union bound—without requiring independence—to select \(v\) satisfying \(1/(4m)\le |u_i^{\mathsf T}v|\le\sqrt{2\ln(8m)}\) simultaneously. The collinear construction then projects under each rank-one metric to an equally spaced scalar grid. Its nearest-grid error is bounded by the grid-spacing term plus \((|Z|-2\sqrt{\ln M})_+^2\); Gaussian tail integration yields \(B(M,m)\). The rank-one water-filling identity \(R_{\mathrm{wf}}(\Sigma_i,D)=(2n)^{-1}\log_2(1/D)\) for \(0<D<1\) gives (1), and the estimate on \(M_n^2B(M_n,m_n)\) gives (2) when \(\ln m_n=o(n)\).

value.title: Collinear codebook tailored to a finite rank-one metric family
value.summary: After selecting a witness \(v\) with \(1/(4m)\le |u_i^{\mathsf T}v|\le\sqrt{2\ln(8m)}\), set \(\alpha_*=\min_i|u_i^{\mathsf T}v|\), \(A=2\sqrt{\ln M}\), \(s_j=-A/\alpha_*+2A(j-1)/(\alpha_*(M-1))\), and \(c_j=s_jv\) for \(1\le j\le M\). This produces the accepted simultaneous distortion bound for the prescribed finite family. The construction is tailored to that family and need not control other rank-one or higher-rank metrics. Its displayed formula is explicit after the probabilistic existence selection of \(v\); no effective deterministic or efficient witness-construction algorithm is established.
